text: Git branching is an important part of modern version control workflows. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to develop and test their changes safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open pull requests so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This process keeps the project stable and helps team members collaborate effectively. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, developers can manage changes clearly and avoid mistakes in shared codebases.
